trials.notes: Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and used only documented calls: next_token(), get_token_type(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), get_current_depth(), add_class(), get_last_error(), and get_updated_html(). The manual list stack is supported by the token-walking docs, but it is less idiomatic than inspecting get_breadcrumbs(); the stored depths are unused, which suggests partial over-application of the depth recipe. Handles processor creation failure and parser errors, but not paused_at_incomplete_token().

Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records. This is the closest to the documented structural pattern: HTML Processor, next_tag(), get_breadcrumbs(), add_class(), and get_updated_html(). The tag_name => null query is documented, though plain next_tag() would be simpler. It checks create_fragment() returning null, but does not define an explicit fallback if the processor later stops on unsupported or incomplete input.

Passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Correct processor and all API calls are documented: next_token(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), add_class(), get_last_error(), paused_at_incomplete_token(), and get_updated_html(). The open-list counter works, including the tested malformed-style probes, but it is a lower-level reconstruction of information already available through get_breadcrumbs(). Stronger than trial-1 on incomplete-input handling.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The docs appear to have done the important work: the Tag Processor "Which processor should I use?" section explicitly says it has no tree awareness and points nesting/depth work to WP_HTML_Processor; the HTML Processor overview says it is for nested structure; get_breadcrumbs() explains the root-to-current path; next_tag() documents scanning any tag and branching on get_tag(); add_class() and get_updated_html() describe safe class edits and byte-preserving output. Near-misses: trials 1 and 3 chose manual token-depth/list-stack tracking instead of the simpler breadcrumb ancestor check, and trial 1 recorded depths without using them. That suggests the token-walking recipes are clear enough to enable a working solution, but prominent enough that models may reach for them when a current-node ancestry API is the better fit. Trial 2 did not spell out a policy for later parser aborts or incomplete trailing syntax, but the hidden cases did not exercise that distinction and the reference likewise returns get_updated_html() after the scan.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say breadcrumbs include the matched element, but they do not make the common ancestor-inspection pattern explicit. A reader can easily forget to exclude the current node when asking whether an ancestor has a given tag name.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note: the final breadcrumb is the current node; ancestor-only checks should inspect all entries except the last. Include a generic example such as testing whether the current element is inside an ARTICLE, NAV, or list without solving this task specifically.

doc_gaps.problem: Breadcrumb queries are documented for direct structural paths, but the distinction between matching a specific path and testing for any ancestor anywhere is implicit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that breadcrumbs in next_tag() express a path/suffix match, while arbitrary ancestor predicates should scan matching tags and call get_breadcrumbs() on each match.

doc_gaps.problem: The depth recipes are useful, but they can draw users into manual stack tracking even when the current-token ancestry APIs already answer the question. Trials 1 and 3 reconstructed list ancestry manually.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add guidance on choosing between get_breadcrumbs() and manual token state: use get_breadcrumbs() for facts about the current node's ancestors; use next_token() plus depth/state when scanning a bounded subtree, counting descendants, or needing closers/text tokens.

doc_gaps.problem: The Tag Processor get_updated_html() docs explain byte preservation, but the HTML Processor docs do not centralize what to do when a structural scan stops early after some edits have been queued.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an HTML Processor note near get_last_error(), next_token(), or inherited mutation methods: after structural mutations, callers should choose an explicit policy for get_last_error() and paused_at_incomplete_token(), such as returning original input, partial queued edits, or a sentinel, depending on the function contract.
